extracted.intended_audience: State MCSAP Lead Agencies, State DataQs administrators, motor carriers and other DataQs stakeholders (drivers, industry organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration proposed requirements for how States must accept, review, reconsider, and finalize Requests for Data Review (RDRs) submitted through DataQs as a condition of MCSAP grant funding. Covers timelines, reviewer independence, documentation, plan submission, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of contact for crash and inspection RDRs
rubrics_metrics.description: States must establish points of contact for crash and inspection RDRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States are required to have designated contacts to receive and manage RDRs to ensure accountability and clear communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal scope for accepting RDRs
rubrics_metrics.description: States must accept and conduct a good faith review of all inspection-related RDRs that are submitted within 3 years from the date of inspection and, for all crash-related RDRs, for 5 years from the date of a crash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the maximum lookback window for State-reviewed RDRs submitted in DataQs for State-owned data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FMCSA policy related to Adjudicated Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: States must follow FMCSA's policy related to Adjudicated Citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States' DataQs processes must be consistent with FMCSA's prior policy on adjudicated citations (see referenced FR notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: DataQs Implementation Plan: submission and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: State MCSAP Lead Agencies must submit a DataQs Implementation Plan for how the agency will meet the objectives and requirements of the Initial Review, Reconsideration Review, and Final Review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must submit an Initial DataQs Implementation Plan that must be approved by FMCSA; updates to the plan must be submitted as part of the annual CVSP process. If changes do not meet FMCSA's requirements, FMCSA will notify the State and the previous version remains in effect until approval. Approved plans would be made available to the public through DataQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: State participation in FMCSA program reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: States must participate in FMCSA program reviews of their DataQs processes and procedures, as required for current existing MCSAP programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMCSA will review State implementation and may require corrective actions or use reviews to enforce compliance with these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: States must accept and conduct a good faith review of all applicable RDRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must meaningfully evaluate submissions rather than summarily dismissing or closing requests without proper review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-level review and escalation structure
rubrics_metrics.description: States must incorporate a multi-level review process for RDRs, escalating the review from the DataQs analyst in the State MCSAP Lead Agency to a responsible decision-maker or panel of subject matter experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each RDR would be evaluated based on the documentation and evidence provided by the submitter, along with any State documents or evidence. States are encouraged to adopt a multi-level review process appropriate for their agency structure to support independent evaluation of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Review: opening and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: States must open an RDR within seven days of submission. States must respond to the RDR, either to request additional information or communicate a decision, within 21 days of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When opened the status should change from “New” to “Open—In Review.” If the State requests additional information the requestor has 14 days to provide it; those 14 days do not impact the State's timeline (the clock stops while the requestor gathers information and restarts when they respond). If the requestor does not respond, the system will close the request with the status “Closed—No Requestor Response.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Review: content required when 'Closed—No Data Correction Made'
rubrics_metrics.description: Each RDR closed with the status “Closed—No Data Correction Made” must adequately explain the facts and analysis supporting the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must contain: Description of or link to the State's approved DataQs Implementation Plan; Decision-maker (name and title); List of evidence reviewed; Decision; Specific reason(s) for decision; and Next steps/directions for more information (RDR Reconsideration process). Also: the issuing officer or inspector cannot be the sole decision-maker when the outcome is “Closed—No Data Correction Made.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of requests closed for no requestor response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requestor does not respond to a State request for additional information, the system will close the request with the status “Closed—No Requestor Response.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request that is reopened after being closed for no response will be reviewed at the level it was closed, and not escalated.

rubrics_metrics.name: RDR Reconsideration: applicability and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The RDR Reconsideration process is applicable to requests that received a full review and a decision during the Initial Review phase; States must open a RDR Reconsideration request within 7 days and reach a decision and communicate it to the submitter within 21 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State requests additional information during Reconsideration, the requestor has 14 days to provide it; those 14 days do not impact the State's 21-day timeline (clock stops while requestor gathers information). Reconsideration does not include requests closed due to lack of information or reopened without a valid reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: RDR Reconsideration: reviewer independence and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The RDR Reconsideration must be reviewed and decided by a person or panel with appropriate subject matter expertise within the MCSAP Lead Agency and must not be reviewed or decided by the issuing officer or inspector, nor a direct supervisor of the issuing officer or inspector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal review should be incorporated, where applicable. Each RDR Reconsideration closed with “Closed—No Data Correction Made” must include: Decision-maker (name and title); Description of evidence reviewed; Decision; Specific reason(s) for decision; and Next steps/directions for more information (Final Review process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Review: applicability and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Review process is applicable after Initial Review and RDR Reconsideration phases; States must open a Final Review request within seven days and reach a decision and communicate it to the submitter within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional information is requested during Final Review the requestor has 14 days to provide it (those 14 days do not impact the State's timeline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Review: escalation and reviewer independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Review must be escalated for review by a responsible decision-maker identified by the State (e.g., Senior Leader in the MCSAP Office) who is outside the chain of command for the issuing officer or inspector, or delegated to a panel that provides a recommendation to the decision-maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels could include representatives from the State's existing DataQs Review Council, CVSA, or the trucking industry. However, the person(s) or panel reviewing and/or deciding the Final Review must not be anyone involved in the review or decision of the Initial RDR decision or RDR Reconsideration decision. The State's decision would be considered final by FMCSA after the Final Review is completed. FMCSA will be available to consult during Reconsideration or Final Review if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof remains with the requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof for all requests within DataQs (RDRs, RDR Reconsideration Requests, and Final Review Requests) remains with the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to remove or modify information that negatively impacts the requester or others will not be successful without factual and/or legal justification of why the information is incorrect or incomplete, providing documentation supporting the request when necessary. Unsubstantiated requests may be returned to the requester for more information or closed with no action taken. Requests closed for no response will not be deemed a substantive decision and may be reopened once a sufficient response is received. For Reconsideration and Final Review, requesters must address the State's factual and/or legal basis for the decision and explain why they believe the decision to be incorrect, with additional documentation when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based evaluation of RDRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each RDR would be evaluated based on the documentation and evidence provided by the submitter of the RDR, along with any State documents or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must list evidence reviewed and explain the factual and analytical basis for conclusions; supplemental documentation may be requested and failure to provide adequate documentation can result in closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: public availability of approved plans and explanatory responses
rubrics_metrics.description: States must submit DataQs Implementation Plans that, once approved, would be made available to the public on DataQs. Responses for closed RDRs must include explanatory reasons for the decision so users can better understand the decision-making process and interpret State conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved plans available publicly promote transparency and reasonable expectations. FMCSA is proposing that responses for closed RDRs include the required elements (decision-maker, evidence, specific reasons, next steps). FMCSA stated that decisions from RDRs would not be posted publicly on FMCSA website but would be available to the parties involved with the RDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: applies to State-owned data
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed requirements would apply to requests submitted in DataQs on State-owned data; they would not apply to federally-owned data (e.g., requests submitted to CPDP, petitions to the Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse Program, or other FMCSA offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes jurisdictional applicability of the proposed MCSAP-related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability tied to MCSAP Grant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal revises MCSAP Grant requirements to provide guardrails for the RDR process and accountability for States; the proposal would impact funding distributed by FMCSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must meet the requirements (plan submission/approval, timelines, participation in reviews) as part of MCSAP grant conditions; FMCSA solicits comment on how States should be held accountable for compliance.
